en: The Verses on the King of Vows of Maitreya Bodhisattva, as spoken by the Buddha;
translated from the Tibetan and Mongolian texts by Gongbu Chabu, Chamberlain and Director of Tibetan Studies,
who served as the Chief Translator for the Imperial Council.
In the Sanskrit language: *Ārya-maitreya-praṇidhāna-rāja*. In the Chinese language:
*Shèng Mílè Yuànwáng* (The Holy King of Maitreya’s Vows).
Homage to all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Mahāsattvas.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya formerly vowed to practice the conduct of enlightenment,"
During the six periods of day and night,
he bared his right shoulder and knelt with his right knee upon the ground.
With palms joined in reverence,
he made this aspiration:
"Homage to all Buddhas and to the seers endowed with the divine eye."
To the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas and the assembly of Śrāvakas,
who cause one to avoid the precipices of the evil realms and show the path to Nirvāṇa,
leading others into the state beyond old age and death— to the Bodhicitta, I pay homage.
Whatever sins I have committed with a mind clouded by ignorance,
I now confess them all before the Buddha without exception.
Whatever merit has been accumulated through the three doors of my own being, [I rejoice in it].
I am of the lineage of universal wisdom; may my path be inexhaustible.
In all the lands of the ten directions, whatever offerings were made to the Buddhas and in which the Buddhas of the past rejoiced—may I now rejoice in them all.
I repent of all transgressions; I rejoice in all roots of goodness;
I pay homage to all Buddhas; May I attain great wisdom.
In all directions and places, To all the Great Bodhisattvas—
Those who abide in the ten stages, please quickly attain equal and perfect enlightenment.
Having realized the mind of perfect awakening, subdue the armies of all māras;
for the benefit of all sentient beings, we pray that you turn the wheel of Dharma.
With the sound of the great Dharma drum, may you deliver sentient beings from the limits of suffering;
May you remain in the world for immeasurable kalpas, preaching the Dharma at all times.
I pray that you exercise the wisdom of great compassion, To mercifully rescue and sustain all sentient beings.
Sunk in the marsh of craving and bound by the fetters of affection,
sentient beings are beset by obstacles; yet the Buddhas do not harbor resentment toward these conscious beings, but rather abandon them not,
but rather uproot them from the ocean of the three realms of existence through their compassion.
All the Buddhas of the three periods of time have practiced various paths and dharmas;
I now follow and study them all, Vowing to realize the path to Bodhi and together ascend to the six pāramitās, To deliver all sentient beings of the six realms.
Having realized the six supernormal powers, may one attain the unsurpassed path;
Realizing the source of non-arising, being without location or self-nature, One awakens to this principle of true emptiness: Neither wisdom nor attainment exists.
There is no life-principle and no sentient being; there is no rejection and no acceptance.
May you aspire to reach the Dharma of non-self, which is equal to the Great Sages and Buddhas.
May you not dwell in the two types of grasping regarding all things that are gathered.
For the benefit of sentient beings, I practice generosity without stinginess,
offering varieties of lavish and abundant goods;
since the nature of all things is empty and quiescent, I fulfill the perfection of giving.
The Chapter on Receiving and Abiding: Flawless and most pure, free from delusion and arrogance, The perfection of the precepts is like earth, water, fire, and wind;
These four elements have no aversion toward contact.
Though provoked by aggression, they harbor no anger; they fulfill the perfection of patience.
From the initial arousal of the mind until its end, they are ever diligent;
with constant joy and without laxity, they fulfill the perfection of vigor through the courageous power of body and mind.
Taming those of the right assembly through the illusion-like samādhi, vajra-dhyāna, and so forth;
perfecting the dhyāna-pāramitā and the three gates of liberation;
the Dharma equal throughout the three times.
With clarity gained through hearing, reflection, and meditation,
you possess the perfect wisdom praised by all Buddhas; with blazing and magnificent radiance,
you diligently cultivate the bodhisattva practices, fulfilling the aspirations of both yourself and others.
Practicing this path to enlightenment, I, a son of Maitreya,
have perfected the six pāramitās and transcended the ten stages (bhūmis). By these virtuous aspirations,
may all sentient beings, at the end of their lives, swiftly proceed to the Tuṣita palace.
May we all take birth within the Hall of Vision, To become the eldest sons of Maitreya;
When you attain mastery on the ten stages and descend to Jambudvīpa To realize the great rank of the Ten Powers,
I pray that you grant us the taste of the nectar of the sublime Dharma, So that we may fulfill the Buddha’s conduct without exception.
When his life here ends, by virtue of his aspirational power, he will immediately attain rebirth in the Tuṣita Heaven;
there he will joyfully serve the Honored One Maitreya and swiftly receive the prediction of his own enlightenment. Ānanda!
It should be known that the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya thus cultivates pure karmic actions through skillful means in accordance with reality;
his path is level and smooth.
Thereby attaining unsurpassed bodhi,
achieving perfect enlightenment,
and accomplishing the gateway of true and great skillful means.
Upon examination, this sutra has not been seen in either the Chinese or Tibetan [canons],
nor does it appear in the Tibetan manuscripts.
Nevertheless, the various scholars of the Western regions...
There are indeed commentaries on it;
for now, let us universally adopt this as a constant daily practice,
together with the *Avatamsaka Sūtra’s* "Chapter on Vows of Practice" (*Bhadracaryā-praṇidhāna*).
The "Chapter on the Vows and Practices of the Thirty-five Buddhas" is known as the Threefold Great Repentance and Vow. I,
an ignorant person, have briefly emulated it.
Generally speaking, when these were first translated from the Sanskrit,
they were largely excerpts of the most essential passages from such sūtras as the *Maitreya’s Descent* and *Maitreya’s Ascent*;
most of them were translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin dynasty.
In the *Maitreya Bodhisattva’s Descent into Birth Sūtra*, it is stated that in times approaching the present, the realm within the seas shall be peaceful and tranquil;
the three teachings shall flourish together,
and provisions for sustenance shall not be lacking.
The people who incline toward the good are many.
Lately, I have often heard of those who organize the Longhua Assembly (Dragon Flower Assembly).
I recall that there may even be some among them who wish to engage in the recitation [of mantras].
I have translated this from the Chinese for the sake of Mr.
Shin’s recitation; I pray that Your Majesty’s compassionate protection be bestowed upon it, and I offer the aspiration that it may be widely disseminated and circulated.
Completed on an auspicious day in the first month of the eighth year of the Qianlong era at the Guangren Maitreya Temple.
